Robust confidence sets under the relative-magnitudes restriction

createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes.Rd

Constructs robust confidence sets for a vector of Mbar values under the relative-magnitudes restriction \(\Delta^{RM}(Mbar)\) of Rambachan and Roth (2023). This restriction bounds each change in the violation of parallel trends after s = 0 by Mbar times the largest change between consecutive placebo periods. The function also covers \(\Delta^{SDRM}(Mbar)\) and the variants with a sign or monotonicity restriction. It takes the coefficients of a fect() run with placebo periods, and fect_sens() in the fect package calls it for you. The confidence sets come from test inversion.

Usage

createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(betahat, sigma,
                                            numPrePeriods, numPostPeriods,
                                            bound = "deviation from parallel trends",
                                            method = "C-LF",
                                            Mbarvec = NULL,
                                            l_vec = .basisVector(index = 1,
                                                                 size = numPostPeriods),
                                            monotonicityDirection = NULL,
                                            biasDirection = NULL,
                                            alpha = 0.05,
                                            gridPoints = 10^3,
                                            grid.ub = NA,
                                            grid.lb = NA,
                                            parallel = FALSE,
                                            seed = 0)

Arguments

betahat

Vector of coefficients for consecutive placebo periods ending at s = 0, then for the post-treatment periods 1, 2, ..., with no reference period. Here s = 1 is the first treated period and s = 0 is the last untreated period. If the vector has names, they must be these periods.

sigma

Covariance matrix of betahat.

numPrePeriods

Number of placebo periods, counting s = 0. Must be at least two, and at least three if bound = "deviation from linear trend".

numPostPeriods

Number of post-treatment periods.

bound

String that selects the base restriction. A sign or monotonicity restriction, if specified, is added to it. This must be either "deviation from parallel trends", which selects \(\Delta^{RM}(Mbar)\), or "deviation from linear trend", which selects \(\Delta^{SDRM}(Mbar)\). Default equals "deviation from parallel trends". See Rambachan and Roth (2023) for a discussion of these restrictions.

method

String that specifies the method for constructing robust confidence sets. This must be either "Conditional" or "C-LF", the conditional least-favorable hybrid. Default equals "C-LF", as Rambachan and Roth (2023) recommend.

Mbarvec

Vector of Mbar values for which to construct robust confidence sets. If NULL, the function uses 10 values from 0 to 2. Default equals NULL.

l_vec

Vector of length numPostPeriods that defines the target, theta = l_vec'tau, where tau holds the treatment effects in the post-treatment periods. Default equals the first basis vector, (1, 0, ..., 0). With one post-treatment period, l_vec must equal 1.

biasDirection

Adds a sign restriction. If "positive", the violation in each post-treatment period, relative to s = 0, is restricted to be positive, \(\delta \ge 0\). If "negative", it is restricted to be negative, \(\delta \le 0\). Default equals NULL.

monotonicityDirection

Adds a monotonicity restriction. If "increasing", the violation is restricted to increase over time, \(\delta_t \ge \delta_{t-1}\). If "decreasing", it is restricted to decrease, \(\delta_t \le \delta_{t-1}\). Default equals NULL.

alpha

Desired size of the robust confidence sets. Default equals 0.05, which gives 95% confidence sets.

parallel

Logical that indicates whether to construct the robust confidence sets in parallel with the foreach package. Register a parallel backend first, for example with the doParallel package. Default equals FALSE.

gridPoints

Number of grid points for the test inversion. Default equals 1000. Fewer points run faster.

grid.ub

Upper end of the grid for the test inversion, in units of theta. Default sets it to the estimate of theta plus twenty times the standard deviation of that estimate.

grid.lb

Lower end of the grid for the test inversion, in units of theta. Default sets it to the estimate of theta minus twenty times the standard deviation of that estimate.

seed

Random seed for internal computations, included for reproducibility.

Details

All restrictions apply to the violation of parallel trends relative to s = 0, the last placebo period. The function differences betahat and sigma from s = 0, which removes that coordinate, and runs the inference of HonestDiD 0.2.8 on the result. Before the inference, it moves the post-treatment coefficients so that the estimate of theta is zero. It adds that amount back to lb and ub. This centers the default grids on the estimate and does not change the confidence set.

With bound = "deviation from linear trend", numPrePeriods must be at least three. This restriction uses the non-linearity in the placebo coefficients to bound the non-linearity after treatment, and a second difference needs three placebo periods.

Value

Returns a data frame with columns

lb

Lower bound of the robust confidence set.

ub

Upper bound of the robust confidence set.

method

Method used to construct the robust confidence set.

Delta

The restriction used, for example "DeltaRM".

Mbar

Value of Mbar for each robust confidence set.

References

Rambachan, Ashesh, and Jonathan Roth (2023). A More Credible Approach to Parallel Trends. Review of Economic Studies 90 (5): 2555-2591. doi:10.1093/restud/rdad018

Author

Ashesh Rambachan

Examples

# \donttest{
  # Placebo periods -2, -1 and 0, then post periods 1 to 4. fect_sens() makes this
  # call for you on a fect() run with placeboTest = TRUE.
  betahat <- c("-2" = 0.02, "-1" = -0.01, "0" = 0.01,
               "1" = 0.08, "2" = 0.10, "3" = 0.09, "4" = 0.12)
  sigma   <- 0.0004 * 0.5^abs(outer(1:7, 1:7, "-")) + 0.0001
  createSensitivityResults_relativeMagnitudes(betahat, sigma, numPrePeriods = 3, numPostPeriods = 4,
                                              Mbarvec = c(0, 0.5), l_vec = rep(0.25, 4),
                                              gridPoints = 200)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>        lb    ub method Delta    Mbar
#>     <dbl> <dbl> <chr>  <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 0.0484  0.127 C-LF   DeltaRM   0  
#> 2 0.00318 0.180 C-LF   DeltaRM   0.5
# }
